newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LINDROS GOAL LATE IN OT LIFTS FLYERS PAST OILERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LINDROS GOAL LATE IN OT LIFTS FLYERS PAST OILERS.

text.p: Eric Lindros scored with 44 seconds left in overtime as the Philadelphia Flyers rallied for a 5-4 victory over the Edmonton Oilers Thursday.
Lindros took a pass from Karl Dykhuis in the right faceoff circle and snapped a wrist shot through goaltender Curtis Joseph's pads.

"I went up the wall, then I skated into the middle of the ice," said Lindros about the goal. "Buchberger tried to pick me up with a check, Bryan Marchment went across the ice and I went around him. I got a good pass and I just went in and shot it."

"It's a joke, Lindros gets away with whatever he wants to do," said Edmonton winger Kelly Buchberger. "He grabbed me with two hands, throws me down. It's blatant interference and Eric got away with it. He complained to the ref for the last 30 minutes of the game and I guess it worked."
Mikael Renberg's goal for Philadelphia with 3:19 left in regulation sent the game to overtime.
Joel Otto and Lindros each had a goal and an assist as the Flyers remained two points ahead of second-place New Jersey in the Atlantic Division and improved to 6-1-2 in their last nine home games.
Ryan Smyth had a goal and an assist for the Oilers (31-32-7), who had taken a 4-3 lead on Mariusz Czerkawski's goal at 4:38 of the third.

In Boston, Jocelyn Thibault recorded 35 saves for his fifth career shutout and the Montreal Canadiens became the last team in the NHL to record a whitewash this season, blanking the Boston Bruins 3-0.
It was the first shutout for the Canadiens in Boston since Patrick Roy did it in 1991.
"It feels good to get one by a shutout, especially in a place where you don't get them too often," said Thibault.
Benoit Brunet had a goal and an assist for Montreal, which won for the first time in five games to move into sole possession of the eighth and final Eastern Conference playoff spot with 66 points.

At New Jersey, Randy McKay recorded his first career hat trick in support of Martin Brodeur's sixth shutout of the season as the Devils blanked the Hartford Whalers 6-0 for their eighth win in nine games.
Bobby Holik added a goal and an assist for New Jersey, which extended its home unbeaten streak to a team-record 14 games (8-0-6) and is 14-2-7 in its last 23 overall.

Brodeur turned aside 35 shots and moved into a tie with four others for the league lead in shutouts. He made a lunging glove save on Keith Primeau's slap shot from the high slot with 15 minutes to go in the third period and stopped Sami Kapanen on a partial breakaway with five minutes left.

At Florida, Ray Sheppard recorded his third hat trick of the season, including his 300th career goal, as the Panthers held on for a 5-4 victory over the Vancouver Canucks, giving them back-to-back wins for the first time in a month.

Chris Wells and Scott Mellanby had the other goals for Florida, which improved to 2-3 on its six-game homestand and moved four points ahead of the fifth-place New York Rangers in the Eastern Conference.

Lonny Bohonos tallied twice in the third period for Vancouver, which had an apparent go-ahead goal disallowed in the second period and is winless in seven straight games (0-5-2). The Canucks trail Calgary and Chicago by five points for the final Western Conference playoff berth.

At Los Angeles, Brett Hull and Sergio Momesso scored 45 seconds apart midway through the first period as the St. Louis Blues posted consecutive victories for the first time since January with a 4-2 win over the Kings.
Chris Pronger had a goal and an assist and Stephane Matteau added a shorthanded tally for St. Louis.
The Blues moved into fifth place in the Western Conference, one point behind Edmonton and one ahead of Phoenix and Anaheim.

At Tampa Bay, Tommy Salo stopped 24 shots for his fifth shutout of the season and Travis Green scored twice as the New York Islanders ended a six-game winless streak against the Lightning with a 3-0 victory.
Salo, making his 14th straight start, had nine saves in the first period, 10 in the second and five in the third.

Niklas Andersson also scored and Bryan Berard set up two goals for New York, which has won three of its last four games and remained five points behind Montreal for the final playoff spot in the Eastern Conference.
